## Choosing a standardization for multiple groups

In a multigroup model, a regression coefficient can be expressed in either
**within-group SD units** or **grand-SD units** for the combined sample.
The choice changes its interpretation. `lavaan::standardizedSolution()`
uses each group's SDs. `R2spa::grand_standardized_solution()` uses the same
grand SDs for all groups. Its original name, `grandStandardizedSolution()`,
is also supported and is used in the examples below.

This distinction matters when comparing a multigroup SEM with a pooled
2S-PA analysis, or when comparing coefficients across groups with different
latent variances (Lai et al., 2023). Grand standardization includes both
within-group variability and variability associated with group mean
differences. It puts coefficients in common SD units; it does not impose
equality of the structural paths or establish measurement invariance.

The function accepts multigroup lavaan fits, including fits returned by
`tspa()`. We first illustrate ordinary standardization, then show the
multigroup calculation.

```{r setup}
library(lavaan)
library(R2spa)
```

The examples use the `PoliticalDemocracy` and `HolzingerSwineford1939`
datasets supplied by lavaan.

## Single Group

For a single group, within-group and grand standardization coincide.
The standardized path from a predictor to an outcome is the unstandardized
path multiplied by the predictor SD and divided by the outcome SD.
Those SDs come from the latent-variable covariance matrix:

$$
  \begin{aligned}
    \mathbf{\eta} & = \mathbf{\alpha} + \mathbf{\Gamma} \mathbf{X} + \mathbf{B} \mathbf{\eta} + \mathbf{\zeta} \\
    (\mathbf{I} - \mathbf{B}) \mathbf{\eta} & = \mathbf{\alpha} + \mathbf{\Gamma} \mathbf{X} + \mathbf{\zeta} \\
    (\mathbf{I} - \mathbf{B}) \mathrm{Var}(\mathbf{\eta}) (\mathbf{I} - \mathbf{B})^\top & = \mathrm{Var}(\mathbf{\Gamma} \mathbf{X}) + \mathbf{\Psi} \\
    \mathrm{Var}(\mathbf{\eta}) & = (\mathbf{I} - \mathbf{B})^{-1} [\mathrm{Var}(\mathbf{\Gamma} \mathbf{X}) + \mathbf{\Psi}] {(\mathbf{I} - \mathbf{B})^\top}^{-1}
  \end{aligned}
$$

```{r}
myModel <- '
   # latent variables
     ind60 =~ x1 + x2 + x3
     dem60 =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4
   # regressions
     dem60 ~ ind60
'
fit <- sem(model = myModel,
           data  = PoliticalDemocracy)
# Latent variable covariances
lavInspect(fit, "cov.lv")
# Using R2spa:::veta() (internal helper; the ::: is deliberate since it is not exported)
fit_est <- lavInspect(fit, "est")
R2spa:::veta(fit_est$beta, psi = fit_est$psi)
```

The standardized estimates in the $\mathbf{B}$ matrix are obtained as

$$
\mathbf{B}_s = \mathbf{S}_\eta^{-1} \mathbf{B} \mathbf{S}_\eta
$$

where $\mathbf{S}_\eta$ is a diagonal matrix of latent-variable SDs.

```{r}
S_eta <- diag(
  sqrt(diag(
    R2spa:::veta(fit_est$beta, psi = fit_est$psi)
  ))
)
solve(S_eta) %*% fit_est$beta %*% S_eta
# Compare to lavaan
standardizedSolution(fit)[8, ]
```

## Multiple Groups

This example relates visual ability to speed in two schools. Equal loadings
and intercepts provide a common measurement scale. The repeated label `b1`
constrains the unstandardized regression coefficient to equality across schools.

```{r}
reg <- '
  # latent variable definitions
    visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3
    speed =~ x7 + x8 + x9

  # regressions
    visual ~ c(b1, b1) * speed
'
reg_fit <- sem(reg, data = HolzingerSwineford1939,
               group = "school",
               group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts"))
```

### Separate standardization by group

Although the unstandardized path is constrained equal, the standardized
paths can differ because the predictor-to-outcome SD ratio differs across
groups:

```{r}
standardizedSolution(reg_fit, type = "std.lv") |>
  subset(subset = label == "b1")
# Compare to doing it by hand
reg_fit_est <- lavInspect(reg_fit, what = "est")
# Group 1:
S_eta1 <- diag(
  sqrt(diag(
    R2spa:::veta(reg_fit_est[[1]]$beta, psi = reg_fit_est[[1]]$psi)
  ))
)
solve(S_eta1) %*% reg_fit_est[[1]]$beta %*% S_eta1
# Group 2:
S_eta2 <- diag(
  sqrt(diag(
    R2spa:::veta(reg_fit_est[[2]]$beta, psi = reg_fit_est[[2]]$psi)
  ))
)
solve(S_eta2) %*% reg_fit_est[[2]]$beta %*% S_eta2
```

### Grand standardization

For each group we have the group-specific covariance matrix $\mathrm{Var}(\mathbf{\eta}_g)$. The group-specific latent means are

$$\mathrm{E}(\mathbf{\eta}_g) = (\mathbf{I} - \mathbf{B})^{-1}[\mathbf{\alpha} + \Gamma \mathrm{E}(\mathbf{X})]$$

The grand mean is $\mathrm{E}(\mathbf{\eta}) = \sum_{g = 1}^G n_g \mathrm{E}(\mathbf{\eta}_g) / N$

The grand covariance matrix is:

$$\mathrm{Var}(\mathbf{\eta}) = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{g = 1}^G n_g \left\{\mathrm{Var}(\mathbf{\eta}_g) + [\mathrm{E}(\mathbf{\eta}_g) - \mathrm{E}(\mathbf{\eta})][\mathrm{E}(\mathbf{\eta}_g) - \mathrm{E}(\mathbf{\eta})]^\top \right\}$$

The grand covariance includes the within-group covariances and a
between-group component based on deviations from the grand mean. Thus,
both latent means and latent covariances enter the calculation:

```{r}
# Latent means
lavInspect(reg_fit, what = "mean.lv")  # lavaan
R2spa:::eeta(reg_fit_est[[1]]$beta, alpha = reg_fit_est[[1]]$alpha)
R2spa:::eeta(reg_fit_est[[2]]$beta, alpha = reg_fit_est[[2]]$alpha)
# Grand covariance
ns <- lavInspect(reg_fit, what = "nobs")
R2spa:::veta_grand(ns, beta_list = lapply(reg_fit_est, `[[`, "beta"),
                   psi_list = lapply(reg_fit_est, `[[`, "psi"),
                   alpha_list = lapply(reg_fit_est, `[[`, "alpha"))
```

`grandStandardizedSolution()` performs this calculation and obtains
sampling standard errors using the delta method:

```{r}
grandStandardizedSolution(reg_fit)
```

In this example, the common unstandardized path is multiplied by a common
grand-SD ratio, so its grand-standardized value is also equal across groups.
For unconstrained paths, the function reports each group's path expressed
in those same units. If a `tspa()` fit has corrected standard errors, the
grand-standardized standard errors use its corrected covariance matrix;
see [Corrected Standard Errors](corrected-se.html).

## Reference

Lai, M. H. C., Tse, W. W.-Y., Zhang, G., Li, Y., & Hsiao, Y.-Y. (2023).
Correcting for unreliability and partial invariance: A two-stage path analysis
approach. *Structural Equation Modeling: A Multidisciplinary Journal, 30*(2),
258–271. <https://doi.org/10.1080/10705511.2022.2125397>
